absent: Direct access device mapping, flush, copy around and recovery write implementations.
Mapping iteration, source map resolution, length query and advance implementations.
Page cache entry lifecycle, conflict detection, locking and dirty marking implementations.
Filesystem specific time update, privilege stripping and version increment implementations.
Numeric values of page sizes, orders, flags and error codes.
Offset limit and destination length validation implementations for remap.
Fault accounting, tracing and page table insertion implementations.
Block size derivation and file size access implementations.

findings.text: Zeroing service for a byte range of an inode using direct access mapping iteration. Caller supplies start, length and mapping operations; helper reports through an optional flag whether zeroing work was performed and returns iteration status.

Partial tail zeroing for a block containing a position. When the position sits on a filesystem block boundary the operation completes immediately without further work; otherwise the remainder of the block is zeroed through the range zeroing service.

Direct access read and write path for file input output control structures. It derives target inode, offset and length from the control and iterator, rejects atomic requests, propagates nonblocking mode, drives mapping iteration, advances file position and returns bytes transferred or error status.
Fault dispatch by page order. Order zero selects page granularity handling, huge page order selects huge page handling, any other order requests fallback to the generic fault path.
Synchronous fault completion. It persists the file range covered by the fault and then installs a writable device mapping for the supplied frame at the requested order.
Equality comparison between two file ranges using direct access mappings. Two iterators walk source and destination in lockstep and report whether contents compare equal over the requested length.
Remap preparation entry for direct access files that delegates all checks and preparation to the shared generic remap helper.

Shared validation and preparation for remap and dedupe. It checks mutability, file kinds, length normalization toward end of file, offset limits, drains pending and cached input output, optionally verifies content equality, validates destination length and marks destination modified.
Post modification helper that clears stripped privileges where needed and refreshes modification and change times.

Mount write access acquisition paired with release. Files already opened for writing use a fast path with a read only mount check; other files take a mount reference, released only when the fast path was not used.
Blocking wait until outstanding direct input output count on an inode reaches quiescence.

Holes and unwritten extents are treated as logically zero. Reads materialize zeros without storage access, zero iteration advances without writing storage, and faults for reads instantiate hole mappings rather than device mappings.

Extents marked shared require copy on write handling before modification. Cached page mappings over the affected range are invalidated, dirty tracking is cleared where needed, and a copy around step preserves surrounding data before zero, write or fault completion.

Reads are bounded by current file size with no transfer at or beyond end, and both page and huge page faults treat positions at or beyond end as bus errors under caller provided truncation serialization.

Zeroing and input output proceed in page bounded steps. Fully covered aligned pages use a whole page zero primitive; partial pages use byte granular direct access with offset within page and per page device offset derivation.

Modification time updates are skipped when the inode carries the no change time flag, when the file mode requests no time change, or when both modification and change times already match current time and no version increment is needed; otherwise update proceeds under mount write access through filesystem specific or generic handlers.
Zero length requests either complete immediately for dedupe or at end of file, or expand to end of file for remap; overlong positions are rejected and empty results terminate preparation.

Range comparison limits each step to the overlap of available mappings, treats paired holes as equal, treats a hole paired with data as unequal without storage access, and otherwise compares directly mapped bytes.
Direct access mapping, zeroing and comparison sections acquire a DAX read lock on entry and release it on all exits, including error paths, with the held identifier passed to release.
Write input output asserts the inode semaphore held for writing; non write input output on a writable filesystem asserts the semaphore held in some mode.
Timestamp update acquires mount write access before invoking the time handler and releases it afterwards; acquisition may fail with read only status on the fast path.
Remap preparation serializes against direct input output by waiting on both inodes and against cached writes by writing back and waiting on both ranges before any content check or length validation.

Mapping iterators are prepared with target inode, file position, byte length and operation mode combining direct access with zero, write, nonblocking or fault as appropriate, then driven stepwise with per segment progress and terminal status handling.

Fault handling derives file position from page index, distinguishes read from write intent, tracks copy on write pages for private mappings, and propagates device frame numbers for synchronous mappings requiring persistence before install.

Page fault progresses through size validation, cache entry acquisition, huge page collision avoidance, per extent processing with major fault accounting for new extents, entry release and tracing, converting mapping errors to fault codes.

Huge page fault in the enabled build validates size, checks fallback conditions, acquires ordered cache entry, avoids overlapping page table state, processes full huge page extents, and on fallback splits the huge page table entry and accounts the event; an alternate build unconditionally requests fallback.

Input output loops over mappings until end or short transfer, handling signals as interrupts, poisoned storage with a recovery write attempt for writes, shared extents with copy around, and zero progress as access failure.
Synchronous device faults return a need sync code with frame number; completion persists the range and then installs the mapping, reporting bus error if persistence fails.
Direct access file input output entry that maps kernel IO control and scatter gather iterator onto mapping iteration and updates file position.
Fault entry dispatching on page order to page or huge page handlers with fallback for unsupported orders.
Synchronous fault completion entry invoked after persistence negotiation to install the device mapping.
Generic remap preparation entry invoked before block sharing or dedupe to validate and quiesce files.
Unexpected extent kinds during writes or faults trigger one time warnings and surface as input output or bus errors, including short mappings treated as possible corruption.

Fault insertion races with entry splitting, conflicting entries or wrong entry sizes safely retry as no page instead of installing a stale mapping; overlapping page table states similarly cause retry.

Remap preparation rejects immutable destinations, swap files, directories and non regular files, enforces offset limits, requires content equality for dedupe, and propagates writeback or length validation failures.
Mount write access fast path can observe a filesystem that turned read only after open and must fail timestamp update rather than proceeding.
Fault granularity contract: order zero denotes single page handling while huge page order denotes huge page handling; huge page fault length is one huge page and page fault length is one page.
No change time property is determined by a dedicated flag bit in inode flags.
Operation mode contract: direct access mode combines with modifiers for zeroing, writing, nonblocking operation and fault handling depending on the caller.
